category: The -ly form that means something else

examples: I could hardly hear her over the music.
There's hardly any coffee left.
We hardly ever see each other now that she lives in Denver.
It's hardly surprising that he quit.
This is hardly the time to talk about money.
"Did you enjoy the meeting?" "Hardly."
We had hardly sat down when the lights went out.
Hardly had the game started when it began to pour.

senses.head: Almost not; only a very small amount or degree
examples: I could hardly hear her over the music.
There's hardly any coffee left.
We hardly ever see each other now that she lives in Denver.

senses.head: Certainly not — used to say that something is obviously untrue, unreasonable or unsuitable
examples: It's hardly surprising that he quit.
This is hardly the time to talk about money.
"Did you enjoy the meeting?" "Hardly."

senses.head: Only just, a moment before something else happened — in hardly … when
examples: We had hardly sat down when the lights went out.
Hardly had the game started when it began to pour.

entries.type: degree — a downtoner with negative force; also stance and time (hardly … when)
entries.position: mid — before the main verb, after be and the first auxiliary; front with inversion (Hardly had…)
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, adverbs, nouns and quantifiers (hardly anyone, hardly ever)
entries.form: -ly from hard, but not its meaning
entries.contrast: hard (flat) = with effort or force: She works hard (много, усердно работает). hardly = almost not: She hardly works (почти не работает). hardly is already negative — I can hardly see, not I can't hardly see — and takes any and ever: hardly anyone, hardly ever, not hardly nobody. Fronted, it inverts and pairs with when (not than): Hardly had we left when it started to rain.

entries.meaning: Recently; during the period of time up to now. ---
examples: Have you talked to Mike lately?
I've been feeling really tired lately.
Lately, prices at our grocery store have gone way up.
entries.type: time — recently, over a period up to now
entries.position: front or end — usually at the end; mid in formal writing (has lately been)
entries.modifies: verbs and whole clauses
entries.form: -ly from late, but it means recently
entries.contrast: late (flat) = after the usual or expected time: She got up late (поздно). lately = recently, over a stretch of time up to now: She's been getting up late lately. Because it covers a period up to now, lately goes with the present perfect — I haven't seen him lately — and not with one finished event: I saw him recently, not I saw him lately. Russian поздно is always late, never lately.

examples: It's nearly midnight — we should go.
I nearly missed my flight.
Nearly 40 percent of the students commute to campus.
There aren't nearly enough chairs for everyone.
The sequel is not nearly as good as the original.

senses.head: Almost; not completely, or very close to happening
examples: It's nearly midnight — we should go.
I nearly missed my flight.
Nearly 40 percent of the students commute to campus.

senses.head: In not nearly: far from; much less than
examples: There aren't nearly enough chairs for everyone.
The sequel is not nearly as good as the original.

entries.type: degree — almost, but not quite
entries.position: mid — before the main verb, after be and the first auxiliary; before its word with adjectives, numbers and quantifiers (nearly empty, nearly 300)
entries.comparison: not gradable — though very nearly occurs
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, adverbs, numbers and quantifiers (nearly all, nearly everyone)
entries.form: -ly from near, but it means almost, not close by
entries.contrast: near (flat) = close in space or time: Don't sit so near; The exam is getting near. nearly = almost: I nearly fell (чуть не упал). nearly the station is wrong — near the station, where near is a preposition. nearly and almost swap freely with numbers and verbs, but only almost goes with no, never and nobody: almost nobody came, not nearly nobody. And not nearly (далеко не) has no almost version.

examples: It's highly unlikely that the store is open on Thanksgiving.
She's a highly skilled surgeon.
I highly recommend the fish tacos.
Everyone at work speaks highly of her.
I don't think very highly of his plan.
The book was highly praised by critics.
Doctors are more highly paid than teachers.
The story came from a highly placed source in the White House.

senses.head: Very; to a high degree
examples: It's highly unlikely that the store is open on Thanksgiving.
She's a highly skilled surgeon.
I highly recommend the fish tacos.

senses.head: With approval; with a good opinion of someone or something
examples: Everyone at work speaks highly of her.
I don't think very highly of his plan.
The book was highly praised by critics.

senses.head: At a high level of pay, rank or importance
examples: Doctors are more highly paid than teachers.
The story came from a highly placed source in the White House.

entries.type: degree — very, to a high level; also manner (speak highly of)
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (highly unlikely); mid before recommend (I highly recommend it); end after verbs of judging (think highly of)
entries.modifies: adjectives and past participles; verbs of judging (think, speak, rate, regard)
entries.form: -ly from high, but not its meaning of height
entries.contrast: high (flat) = at or to a high point in space: fly high, jump high, aim high. highly = very, or with a good opinion: highly intelligent, think highly of her. The plane flew highly and jump highly are wrong. highly keeps to fixed partners — highly unlikely, highly recommended, highly qualified, highly paid — and does not replace very with everyday adjectives: very tall, not highly tall.

examples: We are deeply sorry for your loss.
The plan is deeply flawed.
Many Americans feel deeply about gun laws.
Close your eyes and breathe deeply.
A piece of glass cut deeply into his hand.
I haven't thought deeply about it yet.

senses.head: Very much; strongly or seriously — of feelings and beliefs, and of states like flawed, unpopular and in debt
examples: We are deeply sorry for your loss.
The plan is deeply flawed.
Many Americans feel deeply about gun laws.

senses.head: Far down or far in; to a great depth — also of breathing, sleep and serious thought
examples: Close your eyes and breathe deeply.
A piece of glass cut deeply into his hand.
I haven't thought deeply about it yet.

entries.type: degree — very strongly, of feelings and beliefs; also manner
entries.position: mid or end — before a verb or participle (deeply regret, deeply moved), after the verb (breathe deeply)
entries.modifies: verbs and past participles of feeling and belief; verbs like breathe, sleep, think
entries.form: -ly from deep
entries.contrast: deep (flat) = far down or far into, mostly with verbs of movement and in fixed phrases: dig deep, go deep into the woods, still waters run deep, and in the comparative dig deeper. deeply = intensely: deeply moved, deeply regret; it also goes with breathe, sleep and think. I deep regret is wrong — I deeply regret. For a real hole, They dug deep, not dug deeply.

examples: Listen closely — I'm only going to say this once.
Police are watching the situation closely.
The recipe is a closely guarded family secret.
We work closely with local schools.
Stress and poor sleep are closely linked.
A black SUV was following closely behind us.
The houses on our street are closely packed together.
The storm was closely followed by a heat wave.
The copy closely resembles the original.
It was one of the most closely contested elections in the state's history.

senses.head: Carefully, paying close attention
examples: Listen closely — I'm only going to say this once.
Police are watching the situation closely.
The recipe is a closely guarded family secret.

senses.head: In a close relationship or with a strong connection; working together a lot
examples: We work closely with local schools.
Stress and poor sleep are closely linked.

senses.head: Near in space or time, with little distance or gap
examples: A black SUV was following closely behind us.
The houses on our street are closely packed together.
The storm was closely followed by a heat wave.

senses.head: Very nearly; with only a small difference
body: (очень (похоже), почти в точности; с небольшим перевесом)
examples: The copy closely resembles the original.
It was one of the most closely contested elections in the state's history.

entries.type: manner — carefully; also degree (closely related)
entries.position: end — after the verb and object (watch closely); before its word with participles (closely related)
entries.modifies: verbs of watching, working and following; participles like related, linked, guarded
entries.form: -ly from the adjective close (near), said with /s/
entries.contrast: close (flat) = near: Come close, Stay close to me, We live close to the school. closely = carefully, or tightly connected: Watch closely, closely related. Stay closely to me is wrong. Both are said with /s/ like the adjective close, not /z/ like the verb close (закрывать).

examples: Once the cast came off, I could move my arm freely.
The information is freely available online.
Traffic is moving more freely now that the accident has been cleared.
You can speak freely — nobody here will repeat it.
He freely admits he made mistakes.
The wine flowed freely at the wedding.
They gave freely to the church and the food bank.
The movie is freely adapted from a nineteenth-century novel.
The poem was freely translated from Spanish.

senses.head: Without being controlled, stopped or limited
examples: Once the cast came off, I could move my arm freely.
The information is freely available online.
Traffic is moving more freely now that the accident has been cleared.

senses.head: Openly and honestly, without fear; willingly
examples: You can speak freely — nobody here will repeat it.
He freely admits he made mistakes.

senses.head: Generously; in large amounts
examples: The wine flowed freely at the wedding.
They gave freely to the church and the food bank.

senses.head: Loosely, not exactly — of translating or adapting a text
examples: The movie is freely adapted from a nineteenth-century novel.
The poem was freely translated from Spanish.

entries.type: manner — without limits or control
entries.position: end — after the verb and object; mid before admit and give (freely admits); before its word with participles and adjectives (freely available)
entries.modifies: verbs of movement, speech and giving; adjectives like available
entries.form: -ly from free, but without its no cost meaning
entries.contrast: free (flat) = without paying: Kids under five ride free (бесплатно). freely = without limits: Kids can move freely around the museum (свободно). Mixing them changes the meaning. And Russian свободно говорить по-английски is speak English fluently, not freely — speak freely means to say openly what you think.

examples: It's widely believed that the policy failed.
The app is widely used by small businesses.
Spanish is the most widely spoken language in the U.S. after English.
She has traveled widely in Asia.
The seeds are widely scattered by the wind.
Prices vary widely from store to store.
The two reports come to widely different conclusions.
He grinned widely when he saw his test score.
The trees are widely spaced so the grass gets plenty of sun.

senses.head: By a lot of people or in a lot of places
examples: It's widely believed that the policy failed.
The app is widely used by small businesses.
Spanish is the most widely spoken language in the U.S. after English.

senses.head: Over a large area; to many different places
examples: She has traveled widely in Asia.
The seeds are widely scattered by the wind.

senses.head: By a large amount; very differently
examples: Prices vary widely from store to store.
The two reports come to widely different conclusions.

senses.head: With a wide opening or a big gap — of smiling, and of things set far apart
examples: He grinned widely when he saw his test score.
The trees are widely spaced so the grass gets plenty of sun.

entries.type: degree — by many people, or by a lot; also place and manner
entries.position: before its word — before a participle (widely used); end after verbs (vary widely, travel widely)
entries.modifies: past participles (used, known, spaced); verbs like vary, differ, travel, grin
entries.form: -ly from wide
entries.contrast: wide (flat) = fully, to the full extent: open wide, wide awake, wide open, far and wide. widely = by many people, or a lot: widely known, vary widely. Open your mouth widely is wrong — open wide; a wide known fact is wrong — a widely known fact.

examples: The crowd was mostly college students.
The sauce is mostly butter and garlic.
I agree with you — mostly.
We mostly eat dinner at home.
On weekends I mostly just sleep in.

senses.head: Mainly; for the most part
examples: The crowd was mostly college students.
The sauce is mostly butter and garlic.
I agree with you — mostly.

senses.head: Usually; most of the time
examples: We mostly eat dinner at home.
On weekends I mostly just sleep in.

entries.type: degree — mainly, for the most part; also frequency
entries.position: mid — before the main verb, after be; before its word (mostly students)
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, nouns and phrases (mostly in the evening)
entries.form: -ly from most, but without its superlative meaning
entries.contrast: most (flat) = more than anything else, and the superlative marker: What I miss most is the food; the most expensive. mostly = mainly: The food was mostly vegetarian. What I miss mostly and the mostly expensive are errors. Russian больше всего → most; в основном → mostly. Don't confuse it with most of: Most of the guests were teachers = The guests were mostly teachers.

examples: The doctor will be with you shortly.
Shortly after we moved to Chicago, I found a job.
The last train leaves shortly before midnight.
"I'm busy," she said shortly.
The clerk answered shortly, without looking up from her phone.

senses.head: Soon; in a short time, or a short time before or after something
examples: The doctor will be with you shortly.
Shortly after we moved to Chicago, I found a job.
The last train leaves shortly before midnight.

senses.head: In a short, impatient or unfriendly way
examples: "I'm busy," she said shortly.
The clerk answered shortly, without looking up from her phone.

entries.type: time — soon; also manner
entries.position: mid or end — at the end (see you shortly) or after the first auxiliary (will shortly arrive); before after and before (shortly after noon)
entries.modifies: verbs; the words after and before
entries.form: -ly from short, but it means soon, not briefly
entries.contrast: short (flat) = suddenly, or before the end: stop short, cut the meeting short (прервать), fall short, run short of cash. shortly = soon: I'll call you shortly. cut shortly is wrong. shortly is not briefly: speak briefly = говорить коротко, but She'll speak shortly = она скоро выступит, and only after a quote does it mean резко: "No," she said shortly. shortly ago is wrong — use a short time ago or recently.

examples: The test was fairly easy.
I know him fairly well.
We live in a fairly quiet neighborhood.
All employees must be treated fairly.
The work was divided fairly among the team.
It can fairly be said that she saved the company.
The whole house fairly shook when the train went by.
She was fairly bursting with pride.

senses.head: More than a little but less than very; to a moderate degree
examples: The test was fairly easy.
I know him fairly well.
We live in a fairly quiet neighborhood.

senses.head: In a fair, honest or equal way; with good reason
examples: All employees must be treated fairly.
The work was divided fairly among the team.
It can fairly be said that she saved the company.

senses.head: Actually, almost literally — a literary intensifier before a strong verb
examples: The whole house fairly shook when the train went by.
She was fairly bursting with pride.

entries.type: degree — moderately; also manner (in a fair way)
entries.position: before its word — before an adjective or adverb (fairly easy); end after the verb in the justly sense (treat people fairly)
entries.comparison: more/most — only in the justly sense (more fairly, most fairly); the degree sense is not gradable
entries.modifies: adjectives and adverbs (degree); verbs (manner)
entries.form: -ly from fair; the two main meanings are unrelated
entries.contrast: fair (flat) = by the rules: play fair, fight fair. fairly means either that (treat people fairly) or moderately (fairly good) — position tells you which: right before an adjective it is degree. In American speech fairly good is a cool, limited compliment, weaker than pretty good; quite good is stronger in AmE than in BrE. fairly does not go before too or a comparative: a bit too big, a little bigger, not fairly too big or fairly bigger.

examples: Parents are rightly worried about screen time.
She was angry, and rightly so.
Rightly or wrongly, he blamed himself.
As you rightly pointed out, the numbers don't add up.
The doctor rightly suspected a food allergy.
I don't rightly know where he went.
I can't rightly say when they'll be back.

senses.head: With good reason; justly
examples: Parents are rightly worried about screen time.
She was angry, and rightly so.
Rightly or wrongly, he blamed himself.

senses.head: Correctly; accurately
examples: As you rightly pointed out, the numbers don't add up.
The doctor rightly suspected a food allergy.

senses.head: For sure, with certainty — informal, with a negative
examples: I don't rightly know where he went.
I can't rightly say when they'll be back.

entries.type: stance — with good reason; also manner
entries.position: mid — before the main verb or participle, after be; also in and rightly so
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives and whole clauses
entries.form: -ly from right
entries.contrast: right (flat) = correctly, after the verb: You guessed right, spell it right, Nothing goes right. rightly comes before the verb or participle and judges the action as justified or accurate: You rightly guessed that…. right also means exactly, directly and immediately (right here, right away) — rightly never does: rightly now is wrong. I don't rightly know is informal, heard mostly in the South and rural US.

examples: A good judge treats everyone justly.
The land was justly divided among the heirs.
People want leaders who will govern justly.
The restaurant is justly famous for its barbecue.
She is justly proud of her students.

senses.head: In a fair way; according to what is morally right
examples: A good judge treats everyone justly.
The land was justly divided among the heirs.
People want leaders who will govern justly.

senses.head: Deservedly; with good reason
examples: The restaurant is justly famous for its barbecue.
She is justly proud of her students.

entries.type: manner — fairly; also stance (justly famous)
entries.position: end — after the verb (treated justly); before its word with adjectives and participles (justly famous)
entries.modifies: verbs; adjectives like famous, proud, celebrated
entries.form: -ly from the adjective just (fair), not from the adverb just
entries.contrast: The flat just is unrelated in meaning: just = только что, только, как раз, просто. justly comes from the adjective just = справедливый. He was just punished = его только что наказали; He was justly punished = его наказали справедливо. justly is formal; everyday speech says fairly or rightly.

entries.meaning: In a pretty, charming or pleasantly neat way. ---
examples: The little girl smiled prettily for the camera.
The cake was prettily decorated with fresh flowers.
She asked so prettily that nobody could say no.
entries.type: manner — in a pretty, charming way
entries.position: end — after the verb (smiled prettily); before its word with participles (prettily decorated)
entries.modifies: verbs; past participles like decorated, arranged
entries.form: -ly from the adjective pretty, with y changed to i
entries.contrast: pretty (flat) = fairly, quite — one of the most common degree adverbs in American speech: pretty good, pretty fast (довольно). prettily keeps the adjective's meaning, charmingly (мило). She sings pretty well = она поёт довольно хорошо; She sings prettily = она мило поёт. Before another adjective or an adverb, pretty almost always means fairly, not attractive: pretty ugly = довольно некрасивый.

examples: Surely you don't expect me to pay for that?
Surely someone at the front desk can help us.
"I lost the tickets." "Surely not!"
Without more funding, the program will surely fail.
This is surely one of the best pizzas in New York.
Slowly but surely, the team climbed back into the game.
Her English is improving slowly but surely.

senses.head: Used to show that you believe something is true and want agreement, or are surprised that it might not be
examples: Surely you don't expect me to pay for that?
Surely someone at the front desk can help us.
"I lost the tickets." "Surely not!"

senses.head: Certainly; without any doubt
examples: Without more funding, the program will surely fail.
This is surely one of the best pizzas in New York.

senses.head: Steadily and without failing — mostly in slowly but surely
examples: Slowly but surely, the team climbed back into the game.
Her English is improving slowly but surely.

entries.type: stance — the speaker expects agreement or is surprised; also manner (slowly but surely)
entries.position: any position — front to ask for agreement (Surely you…), mid for certainly (will surely win), end in slowly but surely
entries.modifies: whole clauses; verbs
entries.form: -ly from sure; the flat sure is the everyday American adverb
entries.contrast: At the front of a sentence, surely is not a calm certainly: Surely you know him? shows surprise or a hope for agreement (неужели не знаешь? / ты же его знаешь?) — to open with a plain fact use certainly or definitely. Only in mid position does it mean наверняка: The plan will surely fail. In everyday American speech the flat sure does the rest: Sure, I'll help (конечно), It sure is hot (ну и жара). As a one-word yes, Surely. sounds old-fashioned — say Sure.

examples: I could scarcely believe my eyes.
There was scarcely anyone on the beach.
He was scarcely twenty when he started his first company.
It's scarcely a secret that they don't get along.
A parking ticket is scarcely a reason to move to another state.
Scarcely had we arrived when it started to snow.
She had scarcely hung up when the phone rang again.

senses.head: Almost not; only just
examples: I could scarcely believe my eyes.
There was scarcely anyone on the beach.
He was scarcely twenty when he started his first company.

senses.head: Certainly not — used to say that something is obviously untrue, unreasonable or unsuitable
examples: It's scarcely a secret that they don't get along.
A parking ticket is scarcely a reason to move to another state.

senses.head: Only just before something else happened — in scarcely … when
examples: Scarcely had we arrived when it started to snow.
She had scarcely hung up when the phone rang again.

entries.type: degree — almost not, with negative force; also stance and time (scarcely … when)
entries.position: mid — before the main verb, after be and the first auxiliary; front with inversion (Scarcely had…)
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, numbers and quantifiers (scarcely anyone)
entries.form: -ly from scarce, but it does not mean rare
entries.contrast: scarcely already carries the negative: I could scarcely breathe, not I couldn't scarcely breathe; it takes any and ever: scarcely anyone, scarcely ever. Fronted, it inverts the subject and verb, and the pair is scarcely … when (not than): Scarcely had she sat down when…. It does not mean in short supply — that is the adjective scarce: Jobs are scarce (рабочих мест мало), not Jobs are scarcely. More formal than hardly.

examples: We split the bill evenly between the four of us.
Spread the frosting evenly over the cake.
The two teams were evenly matched.
"Put the phone down," he said evenly.
She answered evenly, though she was clearly upset.
The baby was finally breathing evenly.
The ceiling fan turned slowly and evenly.

senses.head: In equal amounts or parts; spread the same everywhere
examples: We split the bill evenly between the four of us.
Spread the frosting evenly over the cake.
The two teams were evenly matched.

senses.head: In a calm, steady voice, without showing emotion
examples: "Put the phone down," he said evenly.
She answered evenly, though she was clearly upset.

senses.head: Smoothly and regularly, at a steady rate
examples: The baby was finally breathing evenly.
The ceiling fan turned slowly and evenly.

entries.type: manner — equally or steadily
entries.position: end — after the verb and object; before its word with participles (evenly spaced)
entries.modifies: verbs of spreading, dividing, breathing and speaking; participles like matched, spaced
entries.form: -ly from the adjective even (level, equal), not from the adverb even
entries.contrast: even (flat) = даже: She even paid for dinner. evenly = поровну or ровно: They split the check evenly. Same spelling, unrelated meanings. The idiom break even (выйти в ноль) uses the flat form.

entries.meaning: As the final point or item in a list. ---
examples: Lastly, I'd like to thank my parents.
First, preheat the oven; next, mix the dry ingredients; and lastly, add the eggs.
Lastly, remember to sign and date the form.
entries.type: linking — introduces the last point in a list
entries.position: front — at the start of the sentence, usually with a comma
entries.modifies: whole sentences
entries.form: -ly from last
entries.contrast: last (flat) = at the end, or the most recent time: He finished last (последним), When did you last see her? (в последний раз). lastly only introduces the final item of a list. Russian наконец has three English partners: lastly (the last point), finally (the last point, or after a long time) and at last (наконец-то, after waiting): At last the bus came, not Lastly the bus came. Don't confuse it with lately (в последнее время).

examples: You can buy tickets directly from the theater.
The new law will directly affect small businesses.
I need to speak directly to your manager.
The bank is directly across from the post office.
Don't look directly at the sun.
After school, go directly home.
She asked me directly whether I was quitting.
Politicians rarely answer questions directly.
Call me directly after the meeting.
The ceremony will be followed directly by a reception in the church hall.
The patient was taken directly into surgery.
Y'all go ahead — I'll be there directly.
Supper will be ready directly, so go wash up.

senses.head: Without anyone or anything in between; straight from one person or thing to another
examples: You can buy tickets directly from the theater.
The new law will directly affect small businesses.
I need to speak directly to your manager.

senses.head: Exactly in a particular position, or straight toward something
examples: The bank is directly across from the post office.
Don't look directly at the sun.
After school, go directly home.

senses.head: Honestly and clearly, without avoiding the subject
examples: She asked me directly whether I was quitting.
Politicians rarely answer questions directly.

senses.head: Immediately; right after or right before something
examples: Call me directly after the meeting.
The ceremony will be followed directly by a reception in the church hall.
The patient was taken directly into surgery.

senses.head: Soon; in a little while — informal, mostly Southern American speech
examples: Y'all go ahead — I'll be there directly.
Supper will be ready directly, so go wash up.

entries.type: manner — without anything in between; also place and time
entries.position: end — after the verb and object; mid before some verbs (directly affect); before its word with prepositions and participles (directly above, directly affected)
entries.modifies: verbs; prepositions of place and time (directly behind, directly after); participles
entries.form: -ly from direct
entries.contrast: direct (flat) = straight, without stopping or a go-between: fly direct to Denver, buy direct from the farm. directly can say that too, but only directly means exactly or immediately: directly opposite, directly after lunch — not direct opposite. In the US South, I'll be there directly means soon (скоро), not this second. British English also uses directly as a conjunction (Directly he left, we began = as soon as); that use is rare in American English.

examples: Gas prices rose sharply this summer.
The road turns sharply to the left.
Home sales fell more sharply than expected.
The senator sharply criticized the plan.
"Sit down," the teacher said sharply.
Their views on taxes differ sharply.
The photo is sharply focused.
He showed up sharply dressed in a navy suit.
She wore a sharply tailored blazer to the interview.

senses.head: Suddenly and by a large amount
examples: Gas prices rose sharply this summer.
The road turns sharply to the left.
Home sales fell more sharply than expected.

senses.head: Severely or angrily; in a critical way
examples: The senator sharply criticized the plan.
"Sit down," the teacher said sharply.

senses.head: Clearly and distinctly, with obvious differences
examples: Their views on taxes differ sharply.
The photo is sharply focused.

senses.head: Stylishly, in neat, well-fitting clothes
examples: He showed up sharply dressed in a navy suit.
She wore a sharply tailored blazer to the interview.

entries.type: manner — suddenly, severely or clearly; also degree
entries.position: end — after the verb; mid before verbs of criticizing (sharply criticized); before its word with participles and adjectives (sharply different)
entries.modifies: verbs of change and speaking; participles and adjectives
entries.form: -ly from sharp
entries.contrast: sharp (flat) = exactly at a time, or abruptly: at six o'clock sharp (ровно в шесть), turn sharp left, Look sharp! (живее!). sharply is the general adverb: Prices fell sharply. at six sharply and prices rose sharp are both errors.

examples: The delay was largely due to bad weather.
His warnings were largely ignored.
The town's economy depends largely on tourism.
entries.type: degree — to a great extent
entries.position: mid — before the main verb, after be; before its word (largely because, largely ignored)
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, participles and phrases (largely due to)
entries.form: -ly from large, but not about size
entries.contrast: False friend: largely has nothing to do with size and does not mean widely or on a large scale (широко, масштабно). It means mostly (в основном): The movie was largely filmed in Georgia. The flat large is an adverb only in fixed phrases: loom large, writ large, by and large (в целом).

entries.meaning: As the first point in a list of reasons or ideas. ---
examples: Firstly, the plan is too expensive; secondly, it won't work.
There are two problems: firstly, we're out of time, and secondly, we're out of money.
Firstly, I want to thank everyone for coming.
entries.type: linking — introduces the first point in a list
entries.position: front — at the start of the sentence, usually with a comma
entries.modifies: whole sentences
entries.form: -ly from first; first itself is the usual adverb
entries.contrast: American writers usually prefer first (First, … Second, … Finally, …); firstly sounds British or stiff to many Americans, though it is still met. firstly only opens a list of points. It never means for the first time or before anything else: When I first came to Boston (впервые), Wash your hands first (сначала), not firstly. At first (сначала, а потом всё изменилось) is different again.

examples: I'm fully aware of the risks.
The hotel is fully booked for the holiday weekend.
It took her six months to recover fully.
The side effects are fully described on the label.
Could you explain that more fully?
Fully half the students failed the test.
The project took fully ten years to complete.

senses.head: Completely; entirely
examples: I'm fully aware of the risks.
The hotel is fully booked for the holiday weekend.
It took her six months to recover fully.

senses.head: In detail; thoroughly
examples: The side effects are fully described on the label.
Could you explain that more fully?

senses.head: At least; no less than — before a number, for emphasis
examples: Fully half the students failed the test.
The project took fully ten years to complete.

entries.type: degree — completely
entries.position: mid or end — before the main verb or participle, after be (fully understand, is fully aware); end after verbs (recover fully)
entries.modifies: verbs, adjectives, participles and numbers (fully half)
entries.form: -ly from full, with one l dropped
entries.contrast: full (flat) = directly, straight, and in the set phrase full well: The ball hit him full in the face, You know full well what I mean (прекрасно знаешь). fully = completely: fully charged, not full charged. Before a number fully is not completely but as many as: fully 40 percent = целых 40 процентов.

examples: The bone broke cleanly, so it should heal fast.
A sharp knife slices the tomato cleanly.
Natural gas burns more cleanly than coal.
The new buses run cleanly on electricity.
The shortstop fielded the ball cleanly and threw to first.
The update installed cleanly on every computer.

senses.head: Neatly and smoothly, leaving a straight, clear edge
examples: The bone broke cleanly, so it should heal fast.
A sharp knife slices the tomato cleanly.

senses.head: Without producing dirt, smoke or pollution
examples: Natural gas burns more cleanly than coal.
The new buses run cleanly on electricity.

senses.head: Smoothly and without errors, problems or fouls
examples: The shortstop fielded the ball cleanly and threw to first.
The update installed cleanly on every computer.

entries.type: manner — neatly, without mess or pollution
entries.position: end — after the verb and object
entries.modifies: verbs of cutting, breaking, burning and moving
entries.form: -ly from clean
entries.contrast: clean (flat) = completely: I clean forgot her birthday (начисто забыл), The bullet went clean through the door; also come clean (признаться). cleanly = neatly, smoothly or without pollution: The bone broke cleanly. Pronunciation trap: the adverb is /ˈkliːnli/; the rare adjective cleanly (чистоплотный) is /ˈklɛnli/, like cleanliness.

examples: Clearly, something went wrong.
He was clearly upset about the game.
She clearly didn't read my email.
Please speak clearly into the microphone.
The exits are clearly marked.
On a sunny day you can see the mountains more clearly.
I was too tired to think clearly.
She has trouble thinking clearly under pressure.

senses.head: Obviously; without any doubt
examples: Clearly, something went wrong.
He was clearly upset about the game.
She clearly didn't read my email.

senses.head: In a way that is easy to see, hear or understand
examples: Please speak clearly into the microphone.
The exits are clearly marked.
On a sunny day you can see the mountains more clearly.

senses.head: Sensibly and logically, without confusion
examples: I was too tired to think clearly.
She has trouble thinking clearly under pressure.

entries.type: stance — obviously; also manner (speak clearly, think clearly)
entries.position: any position — front or mid in the stance sense (Clearly, …; He was clearly upset); end in the manner senses (speak clearly)
entries.comparison: more/most — more clearly, most clearly, in the manner senses only; the stance sense is not gradable
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and verbs (stance); verbs and participles (manner)
entries.form: -ly from clear
entries.contrast: clear (flat) = away, or all the way: Stand clear of the doors, steer clear of him (держись подальше), The ball went clear over the fence. clearly = in a clear way, or obviously: speak clearly (loud and clear is a fixed exception). Position changes the meaning: He didn't explain clearly = объяснил нечётко; He clearly didn't explain = очевидно, он не объяснил.

examples: He spent ten years in prison after being wrongly convicted.
Many people wrongly believe that bats are blind.
My name was wrongly spelled on the diploma.
She knew she had acted wrongly, and she apologized.
Rightly or wrongly, they decided to sell the farm.

senses.head: Incorrectly; by mistake
examples: He spent ten years in prison after being wrongly convicted.
Many people wrongly believe that bats are blind.
My name was wrongly spelled on the diploma.

senses.head: Unfairly, or in a morally wrong way
examples: She knew she had acted wrongly, and she apologized.
Rightly or wrongly, they decided to sell the farm.

entries.type: manner — incorrectly or unfairly; also stance (rightly or wrongly)
entries.position: mid — before the main verb or participle (wrongly accused); end only with a few verbs (acted wrongly), since after the verb the flat wrong is more usual
entries.modifies: verbs and past participles
entries.form: -ly from wrong
entries.contrast: wrong (flat) comes after the verb in everyday speech: You spelled it wrong, Everything went wrong, I guessed wrong. wrongly comes before a verb or participle: She was wrongly accused, He wrongly assumed…. went wrongly and a wrong accused man are both errors.

examples: She loved her grandfather dearly.
We miss him dearly.
Dearly beloved, we are gathered here today to celebrate this couple.
I would dearly love to see Paris again.
He dearly wanted to make the team.
The team paid dearly for that mistake.
Ignoring the warning signs cost them dearly.

senses.head: With deep love and affection
examples: She loved her grandfather dearly.
We miss him dearly.
Dearly beloved, we are gathered here today to celebrate this couple.

senses.head: Very much — with would love, wish, want and similar verbs
examples: I would dearly love to see Paris again.
He dearly wanted to make the team.

senses.head: At a high cost, with suffering or loss
examples: The team paid dearly for that mistake.
Ignoring the warning signs cost them dearly.

entries.type: degree — very much; also manner
entries.position: end — after the verb and object (love her dearly, pay dearly); mid with would love and want (would dearly love)
entries.modifies: verbs of loving and wishing; pay and cost
entries.form: -ly from dear
entries.contrast: dear (flat, old-fashioned) = at a high price: buy cheap and sell dear. dearly is the normal form: pay dearly, cost dearly — and it is usually about suffering, not money: He paid dearly for his mistake = дорого поплатился. dearly does not mean expensively: an expensively dressed woman, not a dearly dressed woman.

examples: The mayor flatly denied the rumors.
She flatly refused to apologize.
The two reports flatly contradict each other.
"We lost," he said flatly.
She read the list of names flatly, one by one.

senses.head: Completely and firmly, with no room for discussion
examples: The mayor flatly denied the rumors.
She flatly refused to apologize.
The two reports flatly contradict each other.

senses.head: Without emotion or interest, in a dull voice
examples: "We lost," he said flatly.
She read the list of names flatly, one by one.

entries.type: manner — firmly, or without emotion; also degree (flatly refuse)
entries.position: mid or end — before the main verb (flatly refused); end after verbs of saying (said flatly)
entries.modifies: verbs of refusing, denying, contradicting and saying
entries.form: -ly from flat
entries.contrast: flat (flat adverb) = completely, exactly, or lying level: flat broke (без гроша), in ten seconds flat (ровно за десять секунд), fall flat (провалиться), lie flat on your back, turn someone down flat. flatly does the refusing and denying: flatly refused. Lie flatly on the floor is wrong — lie flat. In music, sing flat = петь ниже тона.
